exposure: obstetrician and general practitioner-obstetrician (GPO)-led birthing service
low-risk midwifery group practice (MGP) model of care
Women who had normal vaginal births
Model of care (obstetrician and general practitioner-obstetrician (GPO)-led birthing service vs. low-risk midwifery group practice (MGP) model of care with a planned caesarean section service (PCS))
cohort: 1,172 births at a small public hospital in rural New South Wales, Australia between July 2007 and June 2012
finding: A rural maternity service maintained quality care outcomes for low-risk women following the adaptation from a GPO to an MGP service.
mod_finding: More women in the MGP group had no analgesia or non-invasive analgesia during normal vaginal births, and episiotomy was less common in MGP than GPO.
